title: PB1.3 - 66 Gerrard Street East - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act

stages.body: Senior Manager, Heritage Planning, Urban Design, City Planning
stages.summary:
This report recommends that City Council state its intention to designate the property at 66 Gerrard
Street East (including entrance addresses at 366, 368, and 370 Church Street and 64 Gerrard Street
East) under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act for its cultural heritage value according to
the Statement of Significance which includes a description of heritage attributes found in Attachment 1.
 
The subject property at 66 Gerrard Street East is located on the north side of Gerrard Street East, at
the northwest corner of Church Street, within the Downtown Yonge East neighbourhood of downtown
Toronto.
 
A location map and current photograph of the heritage property are included in Attachment 2.
 
Constructed circa 1855, the property comprises a row of three attached brick house-form buildings,
historically known as 62, 64, and 66 Gerrard Street East, designed in the Georgian architectural style
and raised to two-and-a-half storeys c. 1875 with a Second Empire mansard roof spanning the three
units, together with a c. 1910 rear addition forming a streetwall along Church Street. The property forms
part of the historic context of the Gerrard and Church Street area, at the southern edge of the present-
day Church and Wellesley neighbourhood.
 
The subject property at 66 Gerrard Street East was listed on the City of Toronto's Heritage Register on
November 6, 1974.
 
This property is one of eighteen pre-1870 listed properties citywide which have been identified as
candidates for designation through the City's implementation of Bill 23 amendments to the Ontario
Heritage Act and its ongoing prioritization strategy for listed properties that must be designated or
removed from the Heritage Register by January 1, 2027.
 
Part of the strategy for the review of listed properties on the Heritage Register includes the procurement
of qualified heritage consultants to research, evaluate, and prepare heritage evaluation reports for a
subset of listed properties prioritized
stages.recommendations:
The Senior Manager, Heritage Planning, Urban Design, City Planning recommends that:
 
1. City Council state its intention to designate the property at 66 Gerrard Street East under Part IV,
Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act in accordance with the Statement of Significance for 66 Gerrard
Street East (including entrance addresses at 366, 368, and 370 Church Street and 64 Gerrard Street
East) (Reasons for Designation) attached as Attachment 1, to the report, October 28, 2026, from the
Senior Manager, Heritage Planning, Urban Design, City Planning.
 
2. If there are no objections to the designation, City Council authorize the City Solicitor to introduce the
Bill in Council designating the property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act.
